calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On power play, Dallas sits 3rd of 32, at the lethal end of the scale. Buffalo is 25th, at the harmless end.
calls.call: Dallas’s power play creates more per 60 than Buffalo’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Dallas had 17.7 per 60 and Buffalo 2.2 per 60. Coming in, Dallas was at 8.8 per 60 and Buffalo at 7.1 per 60.

calls.head: Dallas hunts better looks than Buffalo
calls.body: On shot quality, Dallas sits 2nd of 32, at the point-blank end of the scale. Buffalo is 10th, at the perimeter end.
calls.call: Dallas’s shots are more dangerous on average than Buffalo’s.

surprises.head: Dallas leaned on its bottom six
surprises.body: Dallas’s bottom-six forwards played 46% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against its usual 41% and a league average of 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 45 games.

surprises.head: J. Oettinger stole one
surprises.body: J. Oettinger allowed 0 goals on shots worth 2.4 expected goals, 2.4 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 25 starts over the last three seasons.
